State Vs. Upkar Singh Etc.
Fir No. 502 /2009
Ps Igi Airport
 Judgment
(a) Serial number of the case : 45934-2016 (b) Name of the complainant : Sh. Jayaprasad N, ACIO- II, PIS No. 105355.

(c) Name of the accused persons : (1) Upkar Singh S/o Sh.Amarpal Singh R/o F-22, 1st Floor,
Rajouri Garden, Delhi.
(2) Jasminder Singh @ Jassi (Proceedings abated vide order dated 17.11.2010).
(3) Panna Lal (Proceedings abated vide order dated 18.12.2023).

(d) Offences charged of : Section 120-B IPC and 419/420 r/w Section 120B IPC and Section 12 (1)(a)
& (b) r/w Section 120-B IPC.
(e) Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty (f) Final Judgment : Accused Upkar Singh stands acquitted (g) Date of institution of case : 23.07.2013 (h) Date of final arguments : 18.12.2023 (i) Date of Judgment : 18.12.2023 BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR THE DECISION:
1.

In the present case charge-sheet was filed by the State under Sections 420/468/471/120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') and Section 12 of the Passport Act (hereinafter referred as PP Act) against the accused Upkar Singh, Jasminder Singh @ Jassi and Panna Lal.

1 2.

The case of the prosecution is that on 03.11.2009, one pax namely Mandeep holding passport no. H6961715 arrived at the Departure Wing, Counter No.8 for immigration clearance to Milan (Italy) by flight no. EY-211 and he was found to be an LOC subject and revealed that he obtained the passport and visa through one agent Upkar Singh in connivance with Kamlesh Gaur for a payment of Rs.10.5 Lakh.
During the investigation, the pax was found to be a juvenile and was handed over to the Juvenile Officer and his challan was submitted before JJB Board, Delhi Gate.

3. Further, the accused Upkar Singh was arrested and he disclosed that he had forged the passport of Mandeep Singh and the mother of the pax disclosed that Kamlesh Kaur was not involved in sending her son abroad.
Thereafter, verification of the visa was done and the same was found to be genuine and the passport in question was found to be fraudulently obtained on the basis of forged particulars.

Then, the accused Panna Lal was arrested and it was found that accused Jasminder Singh @
Jassi had already passed away on 17.11.2010.
Accordingly, present charge-sheet was filed.
4. On the basis of aforesaid charge-sheet, Ld. Predecessor Court took cognizance of the offences under Section 420/468/471/120-B IPC & 12 PP Act, against the accused persons.
Upon the appearance of the accused persons, charge- sheet was supplied to them.

Thereafter on 19.04.2017, charge was framed against the accused Upkar Singh and Panna Lal U/s 120-B IPC, Section 419/420 r/w Section 120-B IPC and 12(1)(a) & (b) of PP Act r/w Section 120-B IPC, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the matter was fixed for prosecution evidence.
5. During the prosecution evidence, the prosecution has examined nine witnesses.

The entire case of the prosecution qua the accused Upkar Singh for the charge of criminal conspiracy was solely based on the statement of public witness namely Narender Kaur, who is the mother of the pax/accused Mandeep Singh.
The said witness stepped into the witness box as PW-1 and did not support the case of the prosecution.
She has stated in the Court that she had talked to Jassi for sending her son to Italy and he told that, he would charge Rs.9 Lakh for the same.
Thereafter, the witness was duly cross-examined by the Ld. APP for the State.

During her cross-examination, she denied all the suggestions put by the prosecution and did not identify the accused Upkar Singh as the person with whom she had talked on the phone and given the fake passport to his son.
6. In order to prove the charge of criminal conspiracy, it is essential that all the sequence pertaining to the commission of offence while conspiring, is to be proved.

In the instant case, the testimony of the rest of the witnesses does not establish the charge of conspiracy qua the accused Upkar Singh and the only witness on whose shoulder, the entire case of the prosecution was lying upon, did not support the case.
In the absence of the same, there is no incriminating evidence against the accused for proceedings ahead with the trial.

Therefore, in terms of judgment of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration & Anrs. reported as 1996 JCC 507, wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in case where there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction, the valuable time of the court should not State vs Upkar Singh Etc on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108841350/

sentences.text: The accused did not lead any defence evidence and final arguments were heard.
7. Final arguments were heard on behalf of Ld. APP for state and accused.
( 2) Further, in pursuance to the conspiracy, he has dishonestly induced the immigration authorities for giving clearance to the accused/passenger on fraudulently obtained passport.
8. In order to prove the above mentioned facts, testimony of PW Ms. Narender Kaur was elemental.

However, the said witness did not support the case of the prosecution as she has stated before the Court that accused Upkar Singh was not the persons with whom she had made the deal for sending her son Mandeep Singh abroad.
The prosecution through cross- examination could not establish that the witness was won over by the accused or that she has lied before the Court.

In the case of conspiracy, the Court has to proceed with the charge carefully by analysis of the evidence as through the offence of conspiracy, the charge with respect to other substantive offences is also made on the basis of the conspiracy entered by the persons involved in it.

If the testimony of the witnesses is looked into carefully, it can be easily found that there is no document or evidence to support the case of the prosecution that accused Upkar Singh had taken the amount from the mother of the pax or that he arranged the visa or the passport in question.

As the prime witness did not support the case,
thus, the disclosure statement of the accused and the pax can not be looked into and are inadmissible.
The chain of events to prove the charge of conspiracy qua the accused Upkar Singh is not established and in the absence of the case, he can not be held liable for the substantive offences.
9. The judgments referred by the accused are squarely applicable with respect to the present facts and circumstances of the case.
The reference to the said judgments are made hereinafter.

10. In case titled as Govind & Ors vs The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510, it was held that "...In cases where ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak or there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.
The trial should not be Continued only for the purpose of formally completing the proceedings to pronounce the conclusion on a future date...."

Further, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled Ashraf vs State held as follows:
However, in case a witness is completely hostile with regard to identity of the accused even in his examination-in-chief and nothing could be elicited from him to show the involvement of the accused in the offence in the cross-examination by the APP.
such a testimony cannot be accepted and made the basis of the conviction....."

12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Parveen @ Sonu vs The State Of Haryana on 7 December,
2021, Crl. A. @SLP(Crl.) No.5438 of 2020 held that:

entities.text: Parveen @ Sonu vs The State Of Haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "12. It is fairly well settled, to prove the charge of conspiracy, within the ambit of Section 120-B, it is necessary to establish that there was an agreement between the parties for doing an unlawful act.

At the same time, it is to be noted that it is difficult to establish conspiracy by direct evidence at all, but at the same time, in absence of any evidence to show meeting of minds between the conspirators for the intended object of committing an illegal act, it is not safe to hold a person guilty for offences under Section 120-B of IPC.
A few bits here and a few bits there on which prosecution relies, cannot be held to be adequate for connecting the accused with the commission of crime of criminal conspiracy.
Even the alleged confessional statements of the co-accused, in absence of other acceptable corroborative evidence, is not safe to convict the accused."
13. In view of the above, it may be safely concluded that the case of prosecution is not proved against accused beyond reasonable doubt.

Therefore, accused Upkar Singh S/o Sh. Amarpal Singh is acquitted of the offences under Section U/s 120-B IPC, Section 419/420 r/w Section 120-B IPC and 12(1)(a) & (b) of PP Act r/w Section 120-B IPC, as alleged against him.

14. Accused is directed to furnish bail bonds U/s 437-A Cr.P.C in the sum of Rs.20,000/-
ANNOUNCED IN OPEN COURT ON 18th December, 2023 (ABHISHEK KUMAR)
